transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time for this pre-mediation review. As you know, we have a former sales manager claiming unpaid commissions, retaliation, and reputational harm, with a $70,000 demand on the table and mediation scheduled for next week. I have authority to approve the company's final resolution package, but before I set our settlement range or strategy, I need a full picture from both of you. Payroll counsel, I need you to walk me through the commission structure, what was paid, what was withheld, and any discrepancies. Employee relations, I need the full context around this person's departure -- the retaliation claim, any prior complaints, and anything that bears on their reputation. Please be thorough. I'd rather know everything now than be surprised at mediation.

transcript.text: Thank you both. This is exactly why we do this pre-mediation review. Let me synthesize what I'm hearing and think through our position. Thomas, you've confirmed $18,400 in earned commissions remains unpaid, and the settlement authority worksheet calls for a total of $52,000 -- with $18,400 allocated as identified wages and the remainder as general release consideration. Nia, you've given me two critical pieces: the former manager values a neutral reference more than additional money, and the business-unit president has made the neutral reference and rehire eligibility a condition of any resolution. So we have a situation where our financial exposure on the unpaid commissions is clearly $18,400, the president's conditions align with what the former manager actually wants, and the $70,000 demand may have significant room to move if we lead with the reference terms. Here's my thinking on strategy: we offer the $52,000 total per the worksheet -- $18,400 as identified earned commissions, $33,600 as general release consideration -- and we make the neutral reference and rehire eligibility prominent, non-negotiable terms of the package. We present the reference terms early in mediation, not as a concession but as a standard component of the resolution. If the former manager truly values the reference more than money, this package should be attractive. Before I finalize and approve this, are there any other facts, discrepancies, or concerns either of you needs to surface? I want to be fully informed before I lock in our position.
